s2sg.name: Sea to Sky Gondola
s2sg.what: A sightseeing gondola in Squamish: Summit Lodge, suspension bridge, viewing decks, walking and hiking trails. In winter it is also the quick way up to the Sky Pilot backcountry. It is not a ski resort: no ski runs, no ski patrol and no avalanche control.

hours.t: 9 am to 5 pm, last ride down 6 pm
9 am to 5 pm, last ride down 6 pm

s2sg.ticketNote: Round trip. An annual membership costs about the same as a few tickets and includes free parking.
ski: Skis and snowboards go up in winter, conditions permitting, only with your backcountry gear: transceiver, probe and shovel for everyone.
No skis or boards go up when Avalanche Canada's South Coast forecast is High or Extreme.
Know the last ride down and be back well before it. If weather stops the gondola early, you ski down the service road.
s2sg.road: From the Summit Lodge, the Backcountry Access Road (Shannon Creek Road) runs 2.2 km into the upper Shannon Creek watershed, where the Sky Pilot Valley and Skyline Ridge approaches start. In winter the gondola grooms it every day for Nordic skiing, with fresh corduroy for the Friday and Saturday evening Nordic nights. Watch for snowcats on it.
s2sg.terrain: More than 1,300 ha in the upper Shannon Creek watershed, around Sky Pilot, Co-Pilot, Skyline Ridge, Goat Ridge and Mount Habrich: four alpine bowls with up to 1,100 m of vertical. Complex, uncontrolled avalanche terrain: steep alpine slopes, gullies, couloirs, cornices and the Stadium Glacier. Not for beginners.
s2sg.uphill: No uphill skiing to the top: the Sea to Summit trail (6.5 km, about 900 m, ropes and chains) is a summer hike.
s2sg.parking: Gondola base lot on Highway 99: $10 a day (Pay By Phone app or Guest Services), free for annual members. Overnight: ask Guest Services (none on Friday and Saturday nights in summer). The Squamish Connector shuttle runs from downtown Vancouver.
